labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE (de-bridged): MAME runs on the host, no QEMU/QMP, no guest OS, no exec channel. Frames drawshm->shm, keys ctlsock keymap, audio FIFO. Launcher stations/mame-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the golden savestate in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/apple2gs/sta.

museum.blurb: A colour icon desktop on a 65C816 — the Apple II family's last and strangest machine. GS/OS 6.0.1 boots into the Finder in 4096-colour Super Hi-Res, six months before the Macintosh got colour at all, on hardware that still runs every Apple II disk in the hall.
museum.notes: Host-native station: MAME 0.289's apple2gs (ROM 3, 1 MB) runs on the host — drawshm frames, ctlsock keys and mouse through the macadb HLE, FIFO audio. Boots a ProDOS hard-disk volume (CFFA 2.0 in slot 7) straight into the GS/OS 6.0.1 Finder. Third member of the Apple II group with apple2 (GEOS) and apple2e (ProDOS): the same 1977 bus and the same floppies, shown as text, as a monochrome bolt-on desktop, and finally in colour. Pointer is the two-button ADB mouse (8-bit relative axes, MAME_CTL_PTR_MOD=256) — gains unmeasured, so the station ships keyboard-first and stream.pointer.transport stays 'none' until a two-target Finder readback proves it.

reset.mouse: 1:1 ABSOLUTE, closed loop on the guest's own cursor words. MEASURED 2026-09-13 (pointer stream, rig restored from the new golden): the IIGS keeps its cursor at $E1/00E9 (X) and $E1/00EB (Y), 16-bit little-endian, in GUEST pixels -- a live readback, but an OUTPUT: poking it sticks and never redraws, and the next ADB poll republishes it from an accumulator that is in neither banks $00/$01/$E0/$E1 nor the ADB micro's 256 bytes, so the macsys1 abs-WRITE route does not work here. The READ loop does. mame-ctlsock-ram-cursor.patch lets MAME_CTL_CURSOR_ITEMS address INSIDE a save item (m_megaii_ram@0x100E9:2 -- m_megaii_ram is size=1 count=131072 over banks $E0/$E1, so $E1/00E9 is byte 0x100E9) and adds MAME_CTL_CAL_SX/SY so the guest pixel becomes the published one: x = 47 + gx*1.4531, y = 53 + gy*3.325, the measured inset and aspect scale of the 640x200 SHR raster inside the 1024x768 surface. THE RASTER IS LETTERBOXED: it occupies published x 47..976 and y 53..717, so the fleet's corner targets (20,20)/(1000,740) are SHR border the guest cursor can never occupy; the five proven here are the reachable set. FIVE TARGETS x TWO LAPS, arrow tip located on the framebuffer (median of 9 frames -- the GS cursor is XORed in per VBL): (50,56)->(51,57) | (973,56)->(972,57) | (50,714)->(51,715) | (973,714)->(972,715) | (512,384)->(513,386). WORST |err| = 1 px on X, 2 px on Y, and lap 2 was byte-identical to lap 1. RESOLUTION BOUND: one ADB count is exactly one guest pixel, so the loop can only land on guest-pixel centres -- +-0.73 px on X and +-1.66 px on Y in published pixels; the 2 px on Y IS that bound, not drift. A click reacts: MOVEA (105,60) + DOWN1 dropped the Finder's File menu open (41769 changed pixels) and UP1 closed it again. The ADB wire is 7-bit signed, so MAME_CTL_MOVE_STEP=48 is mandatory (120 sign-flips). Binary + golden + fixture are ONE unit: the golden was recaptured on the ram-cursor binary.
reset.keyboard: verified on the live rig 2026-09-08 (golden stream): the generated keymap drives the whole visitor path -- [1] into AppleWorks 3.0 (its GETTING STARTED date prompt, then Return to the Main Menu), [2] into Dazzle Draw 1.2 (title, Space to the launcher panel, Return to the canvas), [B] to BASIC. 40/40 ms pacing, no MAME_CTL_KEY_EXCL, no dropped or duplicated characters observed. Rollover/overlap not stress-tested.
reset.fixture: Apple //e (enhanced) ProDOS boot menu -- a tokenized Applesoft STARTUP program on the /HIVE volume (CFFA 2.0, slot 7) offers [1] AppleWorks 3.0, [2] Dazzle Draw 1.2 and [B] BASIC. Apple II Mouse Card in slot 4. MAME 0.289 apple2ee running HOST-NATIVE (drawshm). Cold boot reaches the menu in 2.6 s; the golden savestate restores it in 0.5 s (MEASURED, golden stream 2026-09-08). Reset is a relaunch that restores sta/apple2ee/golden.sta (the MAME savestate captured at the menu 2026-09-08); the restore was proven frame-identical to the cold boot both in-process and across a relaunch.
